public_body: Brookline Select Board Police Chief Advisory Committee
overall: The AG found the Police Chief screening committee was not a public body under the Open Meeting Law because it fell within the Connelly exception, so it could not have violated the law; complaint resolved.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the ad hoc police chief screening committee was a Select Board subcommittee that failed to meet under the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find that the Committee, created by the Town Administrator to advise him on a task he could have accomplished by himself entirely free from the requirements of the Open Meeting Law, fell within the Connelly exception and was not a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: On further review, complainant argued the committee could not fall under the Connelly exception because its members also served on public bodies subject to the law.
allegations.key_passage: We have found that other bodies fell within the Connelly exception even where their membership included members of public bodies subject to the Open Meeting Law.
